intro: Practice container concepts and commands with matching, ordering and fill-in tasks. Everything is graded in your browser.

labs.title: Container commands
labs.summary: Match Docker commands to jobs, order a first deployment, and fill in commands.
labs.scenario: A developer hands you a web app image. Show that you know the commands to run and inspect it.

activities.title: Command to job
activities.prompt: Drag each job to the command.

items.text: Open a shell inside a running container

activities.title: Deploy a web app
items: Run it detached with a published port
Read docker logs if it fails

rows.label: Map host port 8080 to container port 80 (flag with value)
List all containers, including stopped (flag after docker ps)
Persist data in a named volume called data (flag with value, mounted at /var/lib/app)

hints: Left of the colon is the host; right is the container.
The image must exist before it can run.
labs.review: The run, ps, logs and exec commands cover most day-to-day container work.

labs.title: Images, Dockerfiles and Compose
labs.summary: Match Dockerfile instructions, order a Dockerfile and answer concept checks.
labs.scenario: Review a Dockerfile and a Compose file before they go to production.

activities.title: Instruction to meaning
activities.prompt: Drag each Dockerfile instruction to its meaning.

activities.title: A cache-friendly Dockerfile
activities.prompt: Order the steps so dependencies are cached.

rows.label: File that excludes files from the build context (name)
Command that builds an image tagged web:1.0 from this folder
Command that starts every service in compose.yaml in the background
Never expose this file to containers (it gives root-level control)

hints: Dependencies change less often than your code.
Compose v2 is the docker compose plugin.
labs.review: Order Dockerfile steps from least to most frequently changing, and keep secrets and the Docker socket out of containers.
